c.tagline: Ancient Indian Ocean port city rebuilding behind the world's tightest security.

taxi.fareNote: No meters; agree fare before departure. Independent taxi/tuk-tuk use by foreign visitors is strongly discouraged - nearly all visitors move only in vetted, pre-arranged vehicles with security escort.

emergency.medical: 888 (nationwide emergency line); Aden Adde Modern Hospital, Erdogan/Recep Tayyip Erdogan Hospital
emergency.note: US State Dept rates Somalia Level 4: Do Not Travel; visitors should rely on private security escorts, not public emergency services

avoid.reason: Virtually the whole city is high-risk; avoid Bakara Market and anywhere outside the secured airport (Halane) zone without professional armed escort.
Hotels, restaurants and government districts are recurring targets of al-Shabaab attacks — move only with vetted security and vary routines.

hood_desc: The old city on the Indian Ocean, a maze of coral-stone alleys, 25-plus historic mosques and the fish and produce markets; suits travelers focused on heritage and culture who accept high security caution.
A coastal quarter of faded Italian-colonial buildings near the old cathedral ruins and Lido Beach; appeals to those interested in Mogadishu's architectural history.
The KM4 junction area, the city's busiest commercial and hotel hub with restaurants, shops and NGO offices; best for business travelers needing central access.
A southwestern residential district near Somali National University; suits longer-stay visitors, students and NGO/diaspora visitors seeking a quieter base.

The secured airport perimeter (Halane/'Green Zone') housing the airport, AU/UN compounds and the most fortified hotels; the default (and safest available) base for nearly all international visitors, officials and journalists.

water.note: Poor sanitation infrastructure makes tap water unsafe; use bottled or treated water.

transit.pay: Cash (Somali Shillings or small USD) paid directly to the driver or conductor; no cards, apps or fare cards exist. Fares are negotiated or fixed by informal local convention rather than metered.
transit.hours: Daytime only in practice; travel after dark is strongly discouraged citywide
transit.note: No formal public transit authority; minibuses and bajaj serve residents but are not recommended for foreign visitors due to security risk - nearly all international travelers use private/escorted vehicles

airport.name: Aden Adde International Airport (MGQ)
airport.drive: 15-25 min (convoy/escorted transfer standard; heavy security checkpoints add time)

tip.r: Not customary among locals but appreciated at hotels/restaurants catering to international staff; round up or add 5-10% where service was good.
